title: IDD Domain Model
description: Schema for IDD domain model documents (.model.yaml). A model is one of: entity, value-object (complex or primitive), aggregate, catalog, or a shared value-objects bundle. The discriminating top-level key (entity / value_object / aggregate / catalog / value_objects) selects the variant. Closed-world key validation per #37; unknown keys may be demoted via $conformance.

lifecycle.description: Path to the lifecycle document for this model.

contract.description: Path to the contract (JSON Schema / OpenAPI / AsyncAPI) this model is realized by.

contracts.description: Contract paths this model is realized by, as a list or a name → path map.

rules.description: Business rules. Object form carries an id (the join key cited by lifecycles, features, fixtures, and evidence); a bare string is accepted as narrative and reported as advisory.

invariants.description: Document-level invariants narrative — promotes to canonical from edyoucate-ai usage.

versioning.description: Declares the versioning policy for this model (e.g., immutable, append-only revisions, snapshot-per-event).

value_type.description: Used on value-object documents to declare the underlying shape: a primitive type (string, number, integer, boolean) or `object`. Promotes the primitive-value-object pattern (e.g., email-address as string + format + constraints).

format.description: For primitive value-objects: format hint (e.g., `email`, `iso-4217`). Mirrors JSON Schema's `format` keyword.

required.description: For value-object documents with `value_type: object`, a list of required property names — mirrors JSON Schema's `required`.

validation.description: Value-object validation rules in narrative form.

equality.description: Value-object equality semantics in narrative form.

example.description: For primitive value-objects: an example value.

retires.description: Declares artifacts retired by this model (typically referenced from `specs/archive/`). The closure validator ignores entries listed here.

conformance.description: Conformance tier for the enclosing field. See SCHEMA.md.

constraints.description: Constraint declarations. Two accepted forms: an array of narrative tags (e.g., [non-empty, immutable]) or an object whose keys are constraint names with values (e.g., { minLength: 2, maxLength: 200, pattern: ... }). Both are canonical.

reference.description: Additional reference document(s) for this model.

identity.description: How instances of this model are identified (#83). kind:field names one attribute; kind:composite names several attributes that identify together; kind:content has no field — identity is the canonical bytes, defined by equality. kind may be omitted and is then inferred from which of field / fields / equality is present.

fields.description: Attributes that identify the instance together (composite key).

equality.description: What makes two instances the same. Required for content identity, where there is no field to name (e.g. `canonical-bytes`, `digest`, or a short statement of the comparison).

immutable.description: The identity never changes for the lifetime of the instance. Implied for value objects.

format.description: ID format declaration (e.g., `prefixed-ulid`, `uuid-v4`). Drives ID generation and validation downstream.

prefix.description: Prefix string applied to generated IDs (e.g., `cust_` produces `cust_01HZZ...`).

example.description: Concrete example of a valid identifier.

required.description: Whether the attribute must be present (#82). boolean for an unconditional obligation; `{ when: <condition> }` for an obligation under a named condition; a bare string is the legacy spelling of the conditional form and is reported as legacy-compatible.

required_when.description: Condition under which the attribute must be present: lifecycle states (shorthand for `required: { when: { state: [...] } }`) or a named condition / expression.

forbidden_when.description: Condition under which the attribute must be absent. Same forms as required_when.

const.description: The attribute always carries this literal value.

source.description: Where the value is derived from when it is not authored directly (e.g. `digest of payload`, `journal sequence`).

default.description: Default value when the attribute is not explicitly set.

immutable.description: Once set, the value cannot change for the lifetime of the entity (e.g., createdAt).

ref.description: Reference to a shared model/type artifact that defines the attribute's shape (e.g., specs/models/shared/email-address.model.yaml).

format.description: Format hint mirroring JSON Schema's `format` keyword (e.g., email, uri, date-time).

prefix.description: For ID-like attributes carrying a prefixed identifier (e.g., `trev_`).

example.description: Example value for documentation and seed-data purposes.

itemType.description: For array-typed attributes, the type of each element.

properties.description: For object-typed attributes, the nested property schema.

sensitive.description: Marks the attribute as carrying sensitive data (e.g., tokens, secrets). Drives logging redaction policy downstream.

attribute.description: An attribute definition. `type` may be omitted when `values` (implies enum), `const`, `source`, or `ref` determines the shape.

attributeBlock.description: Map of attribute names to attribute definitions. Attribute names are author-defined; values must conform to #/$defs/attribute.

relationship.description: A relationship between this model and another entity. Either a legacy `type` (back-compat) or an expanded kinded form (`kind` + attributes) — or both — must be present. The expanded form replaces the closed enum from v1.0 (see #38).

type.description: Legacy relationship name. Recognized values are belongs-to, has-one, has-many, many-to-many. The validator expands each to its named combination of (kind, cardinality, ownership). New documents are encouraged to use the expanded form.

kind.description: Structural nature of the relationship. composition (lifecycle-bound), association (independent), aggregation (whole/part without lifecycle ownership), pointer (read-only reference, often to a specific revision).

temporality.description: How time enters the reference. `live` follows the target; `pinned` references a specific revision; `snapshotted` carries an embedded copy; `versioned` tracks a specific version identifier.

statement.description: Long-form statement of the rule; the normative text a checker or reviewer holds the implementation to.

enforced.description: How this rule is enforced (#41). Three accepted forms: (1) a legacy narrative string (e.g., 'persistence'), retained for back-compat; (2) a `pending:` marker referencing a tracking issue, allowed during implementation; (3) an array of concrete bindings that the validator resolves against real artifacts.

pending.description: Tracking reference (issue URL or identifier) for the in-flight binding.

kind.description: Where the rule is enforced. validation → OpenAPI schema constraint, Gherkin scenario, or typed DTO. persistence → DB migration file with a named constraint, or repository typed DTO. invariant → entry in docs/invariants-in-production.md with an emission point in the implementation. domain → unit test or BDD scenario referenced by name.

binding.description: Locator the validator resolves. Examples: `migrations/0042_truth_files.sql#unique-customer-id`, `openapi:#/components/schemas/TruthFile/required`, `docs/invariants-in-production.md#truth-file-revision-pin-roundtrip`, `tests/unit/scan.test.js:scan pinned to revision`. See SCHEMA.md for the format per kind.

condition.description: A named condition under which an obligation holds. A string names the condition (an event variant, a rule id, or a project vocabulary term). The object forms reference a lifecycle state set, an event variant, or a rule id explicitly.
